text.p: Gold, wheat and oil prices staged rallies on Monday in generally firmer world commodity markets.
In Chicago, the Commodities Research Bureau Index gained 0.77 points to 240.49.

London Metal Exchange (LME) copper prices extended an earlier recovery back above the $2,000 a tonne level during Monday evening business, preparing for Tuesday's warehouse stock data, traders said. Latest talk on copper inventories is for a fall of some 5,000 tonnes. Currently, stocks stand at six-year lows of 113,400 tonnes. However, the market is not really responding to the recent run of headline stock declines, with some suspicion over whether metal is being consumed or being moved around from area to area for other purposes. On the charts resistance is pegged at $2,040, and support is seen at $1,985. "As long as we do not get a nasty shock on tomorrow's stock figures, the market seems to be content to straddle $2,000 at present," one trader said. At 1900 gmt copper was indicated at $2,015/18, against Friday's $2,007 close.
Aluminium was quoted at $1,451/54, compared with a pre-weekend level of $1,450.

A technical bounce, a rumor Turkey soon will be in the market for U.S. wheat and some talk USDA will cut the carryout tally for 1996-97 wheat stocks boosted CBOT wheat futures into midsession, traders said. "It's all a technical recovery. The three wheats are feeding on each other," said Skip Searcy, wheat trading specialist for FIMAT Futures. At 1130 CST, wheat was four to five cents per bushel higher, with December up five at $3.83-3/4.

Gold popped its head back above the $380 level on Monday afternoon, showing a brighter face after last week's upside failure. "It's looking relatively healthy," said one dealer. Bullion fixed at $380.50 per ounce, the first fix above the psychological $380 mark since October 30. The afternoon fixing came in 75 cents higher than the morning and $1.35 firmer than Friday afternoon.

CSCE world sugar prices were trading slightly firmer at midsession, but the March contract remained unable to clear the 10.57 hurdle, floor sources said. Speculative buying was met with producer selling at each tick higher, which kept the front month under pressure. If the March contract manages to pierce 10.57 and climb to 10.60, the contract would attract short-covering by the speculators, who added to their short positions last week. At 1140 EST, March was up 0.01 cent a lb to 10.54, having ranged from 10.57 to 10.49. Second-position May was trading 0.02 cent higher to 10.60, while the deferred contracts were 0.01 to 0.05 firmer.
